title: What does the first part of each big-number name tell us?
description: The names million, billion, trillion, quadrillion and quintillion are each a row of thousands multiplied together. We write each as thousands, count the extra thousands, and see what the first part of the name stands for.
teaching_notes: One idea: the first part of the name counts the extra thousands multiplied onto the first thousand. Watch for students who read bi as ten to the power two instead of two extra thousands.

source: A pinch of history: what does the first part of each name denote?
video_script.why: Each international name adds three to the power of ten, so a name is a row of thousands, and the first part counts the thousands after the first.
video_script.substitution: Write each power as a sum of threes, read it as a row of thousands, and count the thousands after the first one.
video_script.anchor: the names million, billion, trillion, quadrillion and quintillion
video_script.payoff_line: The first part counts how many more thousands are multiplied onto the first thousand

final_answer.value: The first part counts how many times 1000 is multiplied onto 1000: bi 2, tri 3, quadri 4, quinti 5
final_answer.spoken: The first part counts how many more thousands are multiplied onto the first thousand. Bi is two, tri is three, quadri is four and quinti is five.

maths_rules: a million = 10⁶ = 10³ × 10³ = 1000 × 1000: the first 1000 and 1 more
a billion = 10⁹ = 10³ × 10³ × 10³: the first 1000 and 2 more, bi = 2
a trillion = 10¹² = 4 thousands: the first 1000 and 3 more, tri = 3
a quadrillion = 10¹⁵ = 5 thousands: the first 1000 and 4 more, quadri = 4
a quintillion = 10¹⁸ = 6 thousands: the first 1000 and 5 more, quinti = 5
check: the power = 3 + 3 × (the number): tri gives 3 + 9 = 12, quinti gives 3 + 15 = 18
video_script.design: Each name is drawn as a row of thousand blocks. The first block is plain and the extra blocks are coloured, and a counter under the extra blocks shows the number.

<bookmark mark='three'/>Nine is three plus three plus three. A billion is a thousand times a thousand times a thousand.
<bookmark mark='more'/>That is the first thousand with two more thousands multiplied on.

<bookmark mark='more2'/>That is the first thousand with three more.
